content.title: Here's the prize money payout for each golfer at the 2026 Texas Children's Houston Open
content.text: We have our story of the year in golf and it's still only March. Gary Woodland, who opened up two weeks ago about his struggles with PTSD following brain surgery, won the Texas Children's Houston Open, his first tour title since winning the 2019 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach. And there wasn't a dry eye anywhere at Memorial Park Golf Course. Woodland shot 21-under 259 total tp top Nicolai Hojgaard by five shots. He will take home $1.782 million from the overall $9.9 million purse. Defending champion Min Woo Lee tied for third place with Johnny Keefer. "Today was a good day," Woodland said. "But I'm going to keep fighting. I've got a big fight ahead of me and I'm going to keep going, but I'm proud of myself right now." Memorial Park, a municipal layout refreshed in 2019 by noted course architect Tom Doak, with consultation from Brooks Koepka, played host for the six straight season. The course is located just west of Houston’s downtown and will also host the Chevron Championship, the LPGA Tour's first major of the 2026 season, next month. The PGA Tour now moves to the Valero Texas Open at TPC San Antonio before the Masters the following week. But as of now, we have our story of the year.
